analysis:
The change is documentation-only in docs/developer/desktop-app.md. It bumps the last-updated date, changes the GUI update-feed description at head lines 106-113, and rewrites the release-qualification bullet (the visible diff places this at head lines ~554-556). The new text says the desktop app uses a fixed https `generic` feed at github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/releases/download/desktop-latest, that release builds (DARKBLOOM_DESKTOP_RELEASE=1) refuse to build without a feed, and that release-desktop.yml replaces that release's assets on every desktop release. It also says the app must never use electron-updater's `github` provider.

No code, controls, or threat-model-relevant runtime behavior is changed in the supplied evidence, and no changed line touches the provider wire protocol, attestation, keys, or cache paths (A-001..A-017, TB-002/003/007/009/011, T-041 are not affected). The T-041 definition supplied is unrelated to this doc change.

Open integration question (unverified, not a finding): the actual feed enforcement lives in desktop-app/electron-builder.ts, .github/workflows/release-desktop.yml and desktop-app/src/main/updates.ts, none of which are supplied. Those files should be reviewed if they are in the PR. In particular, check that the updater verifies code signatures (macOS Squirrel/electron-updater requires signed builds) and that a mutable `desktop-latest` release tag is protected by repository write permissions and CI trust. The feed is a GUI-update channel that is separate from provider attestation. A compromised or mis-scoped publisher could still ship a malicious GUI, which controls local provider operations through the desktop API, but this cannot be judged from the doc text alone. The doc also says the app must not use the github provider and requires https, which is consistent with the prior stated posture. No regression is evidenced.
